**capture_delay**: string type. rule that specifies the number of days in which the capture from authorization to settlement needs to happen. **intracountry**: bool. True if the transaction is domestic, defined by the fact that the issuer country and the acquiring country are the same. False are for international transactions where the issuer country and acquirer country are different and typically are more expensive.

**aci**: list type. string that specifies an array of possible Authorization Characteristics Indicator (ACI) according to the categorization specified in this manual in the section `Authorization Characteristics Indicator`.

method.method: Conditional fee calculations: null is wildcard. Both empty-list-as-wildcard and empty-list-matches-nothing are computed because the manual defines only null. The manual supplies no priority or aggregation rule when multiple fees match; sum, arithmetic mean, minimum and maximum are alternatives, not established billing rules. Unmatched transactions contribute zero ONLY to these conditional arithmetic totals; the actual fee for an unmatched transaction is not specified. All payment rows are included: the documentation supplies no refusal exclusion. Merchant/month euro volume and fraudulent euro volume determine monthly bands. Domestic status uses each payment's issuing_country and acquirer_country; merchant acquirer names do not identify which bank handled each payment. Numeric capture delays match ranges; immediate and manual match their literal categories. Bounds in a-b are inclusive; < and > are strict. Fees are summed at full precision and rounded only at output, using decimal half-even; the manual does not specify tie-breaking or per-transaction rounding.

If a field is set to null it means that it applies to all possible values of that field. E.g. null value in aci means that the rules applies for all possible values of aci.
Monthly volumes and rates are computed always in natural months (e.g. January, February), starting always in day 1 and ending in the last natural day of the month (i.e. 28 for February, 30 or 31).
Fraud is defined as the ratio of fraudulent volume over total volume.

**capture_delay**: string type. rule that specifies the number of days in which the capture from authorization to settlement needs to happen. Possible values are '3-5' (between 3 and 5 days), '>5' (more than 5 days is possible), '<3' (before 3 days), 'immediate', or 'manual'. The faster the capture to settlement happens, the more expensive it is.

**monthly_volume**: string type. rule that specifies the monthly total volume of the merchant. '100k-1m' is between 100.000 (100k) and 1.000.000 (1m). All volumes are specified in euros. Normally merchants with higher volume are able to get cheaper fees from payments processors.

**intracountry**: bool. True if the transaction is domestic, defined by the fact that the issuer country and the acquiring country are the same. False are for international transactions where the issuer country and acquirer country are different and typically are more expensive.
**account_type**: list type. list of account types according to the categorization `Account Type` in this manual

**merchant_category_code**: list type. integer that specifies the possible merchant category codes, according to the categorization found in this manual in the section `Merchant Category Code`. eg: `[8062, 8011, 8021]`.

**aci**: list type. string that specifies an array of possible Authorization Characteristics Indicator (ACI) according to the categorization specified in this manual in the section `Authorization Characteristics Indicator`.

method.method: Conditional fee calculations: null is wildcard. Both empty-list-as-wildcard and empty-list-matches-nothing are computed because the manual defines only null. The manual supplies no priority or aggregation rule when multiple fees match; sum, arithmetic mean, minimum and maximum are alternatives, not established billing rules. Unmatched transactions contribute zero ONLY to these conditional arithmetic totals; the actual fee for an unmatched transaction is not specified. All payment rows are included: the documentation supplies no refusal exclusion. Merchant/month euro volume and fraudulent euro volume determine monthly bands. Domestic status uses each payment's issuing_country and acquirer_country; merchant acquirer names do not identify which bank handled each payment. Numeric capture delays match ranges; immediate and manual match their literal categories. Bounds in a-b are inclusive; < and > are strict. Fees are summed at full precision and rounded only at output, using decimal half-even; the manual does not specify tie-breaking or per-transaction rounding.
method.self_check: Scalar matching and Decimal costs spot-checked; see verification_report.json.

If a field is set to null it means that it applies to all possible values of that field. E.g. null value in aci means that the rules applies for all possible values of aci.
Monthly volumes and rates are computed always in natural months (e.g. January, February), starting always in day 1 and ending in the last natural day of the month (i.e. 28 for February, 30 or 31).
Fraud is defined as the ratio of fraudulent volume over total volume.

**capture_delay**: string type. rule that specifies the number of days in which the capture from authorization to settlement needs to happen. Possible values are '3-5' (between 3 and 5 days), '>5' (more than 5 days is possible), '<3' (before 3 days), 'immediate', or 'manual'. The faster the capture to settlement happens, the more expensive it is.

**monthly_volume**: string type. rule that specifies the monthly total volume of the merchant. '100k-1m' is between 100.000 (100k) and 1.000.000 (1m). All volumes are specified in euros. Normally merchants with higher volume are able to get cheaper fees from payments processors.

**intracountry**: bool. True if the transaction is domestic, defined by the fact that the issuer country and the acquiring country are the same. False are for international transactions where the issuer country and acquirer country are different and typically are more expensive.
**account_type**: list type. list of account types according to the categorization `Account Type` in this manual

**merchant_category_code**: list type. integer that specifies the possible merchant category codes, according to the categorization found in this manual in the section `Merchant Category Code`. eg: `[8062, 8011, 8021]`.

**aci**: list type. string that specifies an array of possible Authorization Characteristics Indicator (ACI) according to the categorization specified in this manual in the section `Authorization Characteristics Indicator`.

method.method: Conditional fee calculations: null is wildcard. Both empty-list-as-wildcard and empty-list-matches-nothing are computed because the manual defines only null. The manual supplies no priority or aggregation rule when multiple fees match; sum, arithmetic mean, minimum and maximum are alternatives, not established billing rules. Unmatched transactions contribute zero ONLY to these conditional arithmetic totals; the actual fee for an unmatched transaction is not specified. All payment rows are included: the documentation supplies no refusal exclusion. Merchant/month euro volume and fraudulent euro volume determine monthly bands. Domestic status uses each payment's issuing_country and acquirer_country; merchant acquirer names do not identify which bank handled each payment. Numeric capture delays match ranges; immediate and manual match their literal categories. Bounds in a-b are inclusive; < and > are strict. Fees are summed at full precision and rounded only at output, using decimal half-even; the manual does not specify tie-breaking or per-transaction rounding.

Monthly volumes and rates are computed always in natural months (e.g. January, February), starting always in day 1 and ending in the last natural day of the month (i.e. 28 for February, 30 or 31).
Fraud is defined as the ratio of fraudulent volume over total volume.

**capture_delay**: string type. rule that specifies the number of days in which the capture from authorization to settlement needs to happen. Possible values are '3-5' (between 3 and 5 days), '>5' (more than 5 days is possible), '<3' (before 3 days), 'immediate', or 'manual'. The faster the capture to settlement happens, the more expensive it is.

**monthly_volume**: string type. rule that specifies the monthly total volume of the merchant. '100k-1m' is between 100.000 (100k) and 1.000.000 (1m). All volumes are specified in euros. Normally merchants with higher volume are able to get cheaper fees from payments processors.

**intracountry**: bool. True if the transaction is domestic, defined by the fact that the issuer country and the acquiring country are the same. False are for international transactions where the issuer country and acquirer country are different and typically are more expensive.
**account_type**: list type. list of account types according to the categorization `Account Type` in this manual

**merchant_category_code**: list type. integer that specifies the possible merchant category codes, according to the categorization found in this manual in the section `Merchant Category Code`. eg: `[8062, 8011, 8021]`.

**aci**: list type. string that specifies an array of possible Authorization Characteristics Indicator (ACI) according to the categorization specified in this manual in the section `Authorization Characteristics Indicator`.

method.method: Conditional fee calculations: null is wildcard. Both empty-list-as-wildcard and empty-list-matches-nothing are computed because the manual defines only null. The manual supplies no priority or aggregation rule when multiple fees match; sum, arithmetic mean, minimum and maximum are alternatives, not established billing rules. Unmatched transactions contribute zero ONLY to these conditional arithmetic totals; the actual fee for an unmatched transaction is not specified. All payment rows are included: the documentation supplies no refusal exclusion. Merchant/month euro volume and fraudulent euro volume determine monthly bands. Domestic status uses each payment's issuing_country and acquirer_country; merchant acquirer names do not identify which bank handled each payment. Numeric capture delays match ranges; immediate and manual match their literal categories. Bounds in a-b are inclusive; < and > are strict. Fees are summed at full precision and rounded only at output, using decimal half-even; the manual does not specify tie-breaking or per-transaction rounding.
method.delta: New cost minus old cost; no absolute value.

Unmatched transactions contribute zero ONLY to these conditional arithmetic totals; the actual fee for an unmatched transaction is not specified. All payment rows are included: the documentation supplies no refusal exclusion. Merchant/month euro volume and fraudulent euro volume determine monthly bands. Domestic status uses each payment's issuing_country and acquirer_country; merchant acquirer names do not identify which bank handled each payment. Numeric capture delays match ranges; immediate and manual match their literal categories. Bounds in a-b are inclusive; < and > are strict. Fees are summed at full precision and rounded only at output, using decimal half-even; the manual does not specify tie-breaking or per-transaction rounding.
method.delta: New cost minus old cost; no absolute value.

rule_cited.quote: The fee then is provided by `fee = fixed_amount + rate * transaction_value / 10000`.
If a field is set to null it means that it applies to all possible values of that field. E.g. null value in aci means that the rules applies for all possible values of aci.
Monthly volumes and rates are computed always in natural months (e.g. January, February), starting always in day 1 and ending in the last natural day of the month (i.e. 28 for February, 30 or 31).
Fraud is defined as the ratio of fraudulent volume over total volume.

**capture_delay**: string type. rule that specifies the number of days in which the capture from authorization to settlement needs to happen. Possible values are '3-5' (between 3 and 5 days), '>5' (more than 5 days is possible), '<3' (before 3 days), 'immediate', or 'manual'. The faster the capture to settlement happens, the more expensive it is.

**monthly_volume**: string type. rule that specifies the monthly total volume of the merchant. '100k-1m' is between 100.000 (100k) and 1.000.000 (1m). All volumes are specified in euros. Normally merchants with higher volume are able to get cheaper fees from payments processors.

**intracountry**: bool. True if the transaction is domestic, defined by the fact that the issuer country and the acquiring country are the same. False are for international transactions where the issuer country and acquirer country are different and typically are more expensive.
**account_type**: list type. list of account types according to the categorization `Account Type` in this manual

**merchant_category_code**: list type. integer that specifies the possible merchant category codes, according to the categorization found in this manual in the section `Merchant Category Code`. eg: `[8062, 8011, 8021]`.

**aci**: list type. string that specifies an array of possible Authorization Characteristics Indicator (ACI) according to the categorization specified in this manual in the section `Authorization Characteristics Indicator`.

rule_cited.quote: The fee then is provided by `fee = fixed_amount + rate * transaction_value / 10000`.
If a field is set to null it means that it applies to all possible values of that field. E.g. null value in aci means that the rules applies for all possible values of aci.
Monthly volumes and rates are computed always in natural months (e.g. January, February), starting always in day 1 and ending in the last natural day of the month (i.e. 28 for February, 30 or 31).
Fraud is defined as the ratio of fraudulent volume over total volume.

**capture_delay**: string type. rule that specifies the number of days in which the capture from authorization to settlement needs to happen. Possible values are '3-5' (between 3 and 5 days), '>5' (more than 5 days is possible), '<3' (before 3 days), 'immediate', or 'manual'. The faster the capture to settlement happens, the more expensive it is.

**monthly_volume**: string type. rule that specifies the monthly total volume of the merchant. '100k-1m' is between 100.000 (100k) and 1.000.000 (1m). All volumes are specified in euros. Normally merchants with higher volume are able to get cheaper fees from payments processors.

**intracountry**: bool. True if the transaction is domestic, defined by the fact that the issuer country and the acquiring country are the same. False are for international transactions where the issuer country and acquirer country are different and typically are more expensive.
**account_type**: list type. list of account types according to the categorization `Account Type` in this manual

**merchant_category_code**: list type. integer that specifies the possible merchant category codes, according to the categorization found in this manual in the section `Merchant Category Code`. eg: `[8062, 8011, 8021]`.

**aci**: list type. string that specifies an array of possible Authorization Characteristics Indicator (ACI) according to the categorization specified in this manual in the section `Authorization Characteristics Indicator`.

method.method: Conditional fee calculations: null is wildcard. Both empty-list-as-wildcard and empty-list-matches-nothing are computed because the manual defines only null. The manual supplies no priority or aggregation rule when multiple fees match; sum, arithmetic mean, minimum and maximum are alternatives, not established billing rules. Unmatched transactions contribute zero ONLY to these conditional arithmetic totals; the actual fee for an unmatched transaction is not specified. All payment rows are included: the documentation supplies no refusal exclusion. Merchant/month euro volume and fraudulent euro volume determine monthly bands. Domestic status uses each payment's issuing_country and acquirer_country; merchant acquirer names do not identify which bank handled each payment. Numeric capture delays match ranges; immediate and manual match their literal categories. Bounds in a-b are inclusive; < and > are strict. Fees are summed at full precision and rounded only at output, using decimal half-even; the manual does not specify tie-breaking or per-transaction rounding.
method.affected_definition: At least one observed transaction matches the fee; for a change, at least one gains or loses applicability. Only merchants with payments in the year can be observed as affected.

rule_cited.quote: The fee then is provided by `fee = fixed_amount + rate * transaction_value / 10000`.
If a field is set to null it means that it applies to all possible values of that field. E.g. null value in aci means that the rules applies for all possible values of aci.
Monthly volumes and rates are computed always in natural months (e.g. January, February), starting always in day 1 and ending in the last natural day of the month (i.e. 28 for February, 30 or 31).
Fraud is defined as the ratio of fraudulent volume over total volume.

**capture_delay**: string type. rule that specifies the number of days in which the capture from authorization to settlement needs to happen. Possible values are '3-5' (between 3 and 5 days), '>5' (more than 5 days is possible), '<3' (before 3 days), 'immediate', or 'manual'. The faster the capture to settlement happens, the more expensive it is.

**monthly_volume**: string type. rule that specifies the monthly total volume of the merchant. '100k-1m' is between 100.000 (100k) and 1.000.000 (1m). All volumes are specified in euros. Normally merchants with higher volume are able to get cheaper fees from payments processors.

**intracountry**: bool. True if the transaction is domestic, defined by the fact that the issuer country and the acquiring country are the same. False are for international transactions where the issuer country and acquirer country are different and typically are more expensive.
**account_type**: list type. list of account types according to the categorization `Account Type` in this manual

**merchant_category_code**: list type. integer that specifies the possible merchant category codes, according to the categorization found in this manual in the section `Merchant Category Code`. eg: `[8062, 8011, 8021]`.

**aci**: list type. string that specifies an array of possible Authorization Characteristics Indicator (ACI) according to the categorization specified in this manual in the section `Authorization Characteristics Indicator`.

method.method: Conditional fee calculations: null is wildcard. Both empty-list-as-wildcard and empty-list-matches-nothing are computed because the manual defines only null. The manual supplies no priority or aggregation rule when multiple fees match; sum, arithmetic mean, minimum and maximum are alternatives, not established billing rules. Unmatched transactions contribute zero ONLY to these conditional arithmetic totals; the actual fee for an unmatched transaction is not specified. All payment rows are included: the documentation supplies no refusal exclusion. Merchant/month euro volume and fraudulent euro volume determine monthly bands. Domestic status uses each payment's issuing_country and acquirer_country; merchant acquirer names do not identify which bank handled each payment. Numeric capture delays match ranges; immediate and manual match their literal categories. Bounds in a-b are inclusive; < and > are strict. Fees are summed at full precision and rounded only at output, using decimal half-even; the manual does not specify tie-breaking or per-transaction rounding.

Unmatched transactions contribute zero ONLY to these conditional arithmetic totals; the actual fee for an unmatched transaction is not specified. All payment rows are included: the documentation supplies no refusal exclusion. Merchant/month euro volume and fraudulent euro volume determine monthly bands. Domestic status uses each payment's issuing_country and acquirer_country; merchant acquirer names do not identify which bank handled each payment. Numeric capture delays match ranges; immediate and manual match their literal categories. Bounds in a-b are inclusive; < and > are strict. Fees are summed at full precision and rounded only at output, using decimal half-even; the manual does not specify tie-breaking or per-transaction rounding.

rule_cited.quote: The fee then is provided by `fee = fixed_amount + rate * transaction_value / 10000`.
If a field is set to null it means that it applies to all possible values of that field. E.g. null value in aci means that the rules applies for all possible values of aci.
Monthly volumes and rates are computed always in natural months (e.g. January, February), starting always in day 1 and ending in the last natural day of the month (i.e. 28 for February, 30 or 31).
Fraud is defined as the ratio of fraudulent volume over total volume.

**capture_delay**: string type. rule that specifies the number of days in which the capture from authorization to settlement needs to happen. Possible values are '3-5' (between 3 and 5 days), '>5' (more than 5 days is possible), '<3' (before 3 days), 'immediate', or 'manual'. The faster the capture to settlement happens, the more expensive it is.

**monthly_volume**: string type. rule that specifies the monthly total volume of the merchant. '100k-1m' is between 100.000 (100k) and 1.000.000 (1m). All volumes are specified in euros. Normally merchants with higher volume are able to get cheaper fees from payments processors.

**intracountry**: bool. True if the transaction is domestic, defined by the fact that the issuer country and the acquiring country are the same. False are for international transactions where the issuer country and acquirer country are different and typically are more expensive.
**account_type**: list type. list of account types according to the categorization `Account Type` in this manual

**merchant_category_code**: list type. integer that specifies the possible merchant category codes, according to the categorization found in this manual in the section `Merchant Category Code`. eg: `[8062, 8011, 8021]`.

**aci**: list type. string that specifies an array of possible Authorization Characteristics Indicator (ACI) according to the categorization specified in this manual in the section `Authorization Characteristics Indicator`.

rule_cited.quote: The fee then is provided by `fee = fixed_amount + rate * transaction_value / 10000`.
If a field is set to null it means that it applies to all possible values of that field. E.g. null value in aci means that the rules applies for all possible values of aci.
Monthly volumes and rates are computed always in natural months (e.g. January, February), starting always in day 1 and ending in the last natural day of the month (i.e. 28 for February, 30 or 31).
Fraud is defined as the ratio of fraudulent volume over total volume.

**capture_delay**: string type. rule that specifies the number of days in which the capture from authorization to settlement needs to happen. Possible values are '3-5' (between 3 and 5 days), '>5' (more than 5 days is possible), '<3' (before 3 days), 'immediate', or 'manual'. The faster the capture to settlement happens, the more expensive it is.

**monthly_volume**: string type. rule that specifies the monthly total volume of the merchant. '100k-1m' is between 100.000 (100k) and 1.000.000 (1m). All volumes are specified in euros. Normally merchants with higher volume are able to get cheaper fees from payments processors.

**intracountry**: bool. True if the transaction is domestic, defined by the fact that the issuer country and the acquiring country are the same. False are for international transactions where the issuer country and acquirer country are different and typically are more expensive.
**account_type**: list type. list of account types according to the categorization `Account Type` in this manual

**merchant_category_code**: list type. integer that specifies the possible merchant category codes, according to the categorization found in this manual in the section `Merchant Category Code`. eg: `[8062, 8011, 8021]`.

**aci**: list type. string that specifies an array of possible Authorization Characteristics Indicator (ACI) according to the categorization specified in this manual in the section `Authorization Characteristics Indicator`.

method.method: Conditional fee calculations: null is wildcard. Both empty-list-as-wildcard and empty-list-matches-nothing are computed because the manual defines only null. The manual supplies no priority or aggregation rule when multiple fees match; sum, arithmetic mean, minimum and maximum are alternatives, not established billing rules. Unmatched transactions contribute zero ONLY to these conditional arithmetic totals; the actual fee for an unmatched transaction is not specified. All payment rows are included: the documentation supplies no refusal exclusion. Merchant/month euro volume and fraudulent euro volume determine monthly bands. Domestic status uses each payment's issuing_country and acquirer_country; merchant acquirer names do not identify which bank handled each payment. Numeric capture delays match ranges; immediate and manual match their literal categories. Bounds in a-b are inclusive; < and > are strict. Fees are summed at full precision and rounded only at output, using decimal half-even; the manual does not specify tie-breaking or per-transaction rounding.

rule_cited.quote: The fee then is provided by `fee = fixed_amount + rate * transaction_value / 10000`.
If a field is set to null it means that it applies to all possible values of that field. E.g. null value in aci means that the rules applies for all possible values of aci.
Monthly volumes and rates are computed always in natural months (e.g. January, February), starting always in day 1 and ending in the last natural day of the month (i.e. 28 for February, 30 or 31).
Fraud is defined as the ratio of fraudulent volume over total volume.

**capture_delay**: string type. rule that specifies the number of days in which the capture from authorization to settlement needs to happen. Possible values are '3-5' (between 3 and 5 days), '>5' (more than 5 days is possible), '<3' (before 3 days), 'immediate', or 'manual'. The faster the capture to settlement happens, the more expensive it is.

**monthly_volume**: string type. rule that specifies the monthly total volume of the merchant. '100k-1m' is between 100.000 (100k) and 1.000.000 (1m). All volumes are specified in euros. Normally merchants with higher volume are able to get cheaper fees from payments processors.

**intracountry**: bool. True if the transaction is domestic, defined by the fact that the issuer country and the acquiring country are the same. False are for international transactions where the issuer country and acquirer country are different and typically are more expensive.

**merchant_category_code**: list type. integer that specifies the possible merchant category codes, according to the categorization found in this manual in the section `Merchant Category Code`. eg: `[8062, 8011, 8021]`.

method.method: Conditional fee calculations: null is wildcard. Both empty-list-as-wildcard and empty-list-matches-nothing are computed because the manual defines only null. The manual supplies no priority or aggregation rule when multiple fees match; sum, arithmetic mean, minimum and maximum are alternatives, not established billing rules. Unmatched transactions contribute zero ONLY to these conditional arithmetic totals; the actual fee for an unmatched transaction is not specified. All payment rows are included: the documentation supplies no refusal exclusion. Merchant/month euro volume and fraudulent euro volume determine monthly bands. Domestic status uses each payment's issuing_country and acquirer_country; merchant acquirer names do not identify which bank handled each payment. Numeric capture delays match ranges; immediate and manual match their literal categories. Bounds in a-b are inclusive; < and > are strict. Fees are summed at full precision and rounded only at output, using decimal half-even; the manual does not specify tie-breaking or per-transaction rounding.

rule_cited.quote: The fee then is provided by `fee = fixed_amount + rate * transaction_value / 10000`.
If a field is set to null it means that it applies to all possible values of that field. E.g. null value in aci means that the rules applies for all possible values of aci.
Monthly volumes and rates are computed always in natural months (e.g. January, February), starting always in day 1 and ending in the last natural day of the month (i.e. 28 for February, 30 or 31).
Fraud is defined as the ratio of fraudulent volume over total volume.

**capture_delay**: string type. rule that specifies the number of days in which the capture from authorization to settlement needs to happen. Possible values are '3-5' (between 3 and 5 days), '>5' (more than 5 days is possible), '<3' (before 3 days), 'immediate', or 'manual'. The faster the capture to settlement happens, the more expensive it is.

**monthly_volume**: string type. rule that specifies the monthly total volume of the merchant. '100k-1m' is between 100.000 (100k) and 1.000.000 (1m). All volumes are specified in euros. Normally merchants with higher volume are able to get cheaper fees from payments processors.

**intracountry**: bool. True if the transaction is domestic, defined by the fact that the issuer country and the acquiring country are the same. False are for international transactions where the issuer country and acquirer country are different and typically are more expensive.
**account_type**: list type. list of account types according to the categorization `Account Type` in this manual

**merchant_category_code**: list type. integer that specifies the possible merchant category codes, according to the categorization found in this manual in the section `Merchant Category Code`. eg: `[8062, 8011, 8021]`.

**aci**: list type. string that specifies an array of possible Authorization Characteristics Indicator (ACI) according to the categorization specified in this manual in the section `Authorization Characteristics Indicator`.

Unmatched transactions contribute zero ONLY to these conditional arithmetic totals; the actual fee for an unmatched transaction is not specified.
